description:
🚀 𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶 – 𝗖𝗼𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝟮 | 𝗣𝗵𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝟯 𝗕𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗻𝘀
From learning open source to contributing to technology used across the Wikimedia ecosystem. 🌍

A new chapter of my open-source journey has officially begun with Phase 3 of Road to Wiki – Cohort 2, a program by Wikiclub Tech India (Part of OKI-IIITH).

The first session of Phase 3, conducted for Group 3, was led by Sarthak Singh Sir, Shivaansh Singh Sir, and Dev Jadiya Sir, and set the direction for what lies ahead — understanding the right practices, expectations, contribution guidelines, and the mindset required to work effectively within the Wikimedia community.

What makes Phase 3 particularly exciting is the shift from learning about open source to working towards meaningful upstream contributions.

𝗗𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘄𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗹𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝗶𝘀𝘀𝘂𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴:
🔹 Wikispeech and its extension/backend ecosystem
🔹 Translation and localization workflows
🔹 Internationalization (i18n) and making interface text translatable
🔹 Accessibility and UI improvements
🔹 Documentation contributions
🔹 Identifying and working on reproducible bugs
🔹 Understanding Wikimedia extensions and their development setup
🔹 Learning how to evaluate issues and choose beginner-friendly yet meaningful contributions

One thing that stood out to me was the scale of these contributions.
The work we undertake during this phase is not simply another college assignment or a project that stays within a classroom. We are learning to 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶𝗺��𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗽𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗯𝘆 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗴𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆.
That brings a different level of responsibility.

It means learning to read an existing codebase instead of always starting from scratch, understanding community requirements before writing code, following contribution standards, collaborating with maintainers, documenting our work properly, and most importantly — building something that can actually be useful beyond ourselves.
Excited for the work, challenges, and contributions ahead. 🌍💻

𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗱𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 | 𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟭 — 𝗪𝗲𝗹𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲, 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 & 𝗖𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗯𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲

Almost 8–10 months ago, my journey with 𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶, 𝗖𝗼𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝟮 began.
What started with Phase 1 gradually moved through Phase 2 and Phase 3, bringing months of learning, contributions, challenges, mentorship, collaboration, and community experiences. And after this long journey, we finally came together in 𝗚𝘂𝗿𝘂𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗱𝘂𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲.

Travelling from 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝘆𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗷 𝘁𝗼 𝗚𝘂𝗿𝘂𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗳𝘂𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲-𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 was itself a memorable milestone. After spending months contributing and interacting with the community online, getting the opportunity to finally meet everyone in person made the experience even more special.

𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟭 — Welcome, Connect & Celebrate
Day 1 was all about coming together, celebrating the journey, and creating new memories. The evening included the opening ceremony, the keynote “Beyond Road to Wiki,” networking activities, learning sessions, reward distribution, fun activities, and the Robo Build amp; Assembly Challenge.

𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗮𝘀 𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗠𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿
One of the biggest highlights of the day for me was being recognised with three awards, including 𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗠𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿, for my contributions and participation throughout the journey.

Receiving these recognitions after months of work made the moment especially meaningful. They were not just awards, but a reminder of the journey, effort, and people who were part of it.
But beyond the awards, the best part of Day 1 was the people.I finally got to meet T, Hridyesh Shivaansh, Harsh, Adarsh, Shrey, Kavaljeet, Tejinder, Dev, Anushka , Arohi, Priyanshika, Neelima, Sanskar  and many other amazing contributors and community members in person.People I had previously known through online conversations and the community were now sitting together, sharing stories, discussing our experiences, learning from each other, and celebrating how far we had come.That is what makes the open-source community special.

It has been a journey from learning to contributing, from contributing to connecting, and from connecting to becoming part of a community.

A heartfelt thank you to Ankit sir, The Open Knowledge Initiatives - India, International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad (IIITH), Wikiclub Tech India (Part of OKI-IIITH)ia, the Wikimedia Foundationn, all the mentors, organisers, contributors, and everyone who made this journey possible.And to everyone I met along the way — thank you for making this journey memorable.

𝗔 𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗯𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆
𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗗𝗮𝘆 at United Institute of Technology, Prayagraj, organized by WikiClub Tech-UIT in collaboration with GDG on Campus- United Institute of Technology , was a memorable experience and an important milestone in my open-source journey.

One of the highlights of the day was being recognized for 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝟭𝘀𝘁 𝗥𝗮𝗻𝗸 in the WikiClub Tech-UIT 𝟭-𝗪𝗲𝗲𝗸 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗼𝗻. It was rewarding to see the efforts and contributions made during the marathon being acknowledged.

𝗜 𝗮𝗹𝘀𝗼 𝗵𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝘀𝘁𝘂𝗱𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 — sharing what open source really means, how beginners can get started, how contributions work, and why contributing to real-world projects can be such an important part of a developer’s growth.

What made the event even more meaningful was the opportunity to meet and interact with Ankit Sir, Shivaansh Sir, Reeti Ma’am,Adarsh Sir, Manvi Ma’am,Arpita Ma’am and many other members and contributors from the community. Every conversation, interaction, and shared experience added something valuable to the day.

A sincere thank you to the entire WikiClub Tech-UIT and GDG on Campus- United Institute of Technology teams for organizing such a meaningful initiative and for continuously creating opportunities for students to learn, contribute, and connect with the open-source ecosystem.

There was also a bittersweet feeling throughout the day, knowing that this was the last event of the current Wikiclub Tech India (Part of OKI-IIITH) Tech team. After all the sessions, contributions, collaborations, and memories, it was not easy to see this chapter come to an end.

I’m genuinely grateful to have been a part of this journey —𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗮𝘀 𝗮 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗮𝘀 𝗮 𝟭𝘀𝘁-𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗸 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗼𝗿, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗮𝘀 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝗵𝗮𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘀.

One chapter may be ending, but the culture of contribution continues.

description:
[𝗥𝗧𝗪] 𝗨𝗻𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁 (𝗨𝗖𝗼𝗖) 𝗦𝘆𝗻𝗰
Today, while returning from college, I received the link for the [RTW] Universal Code of Conduct (UCoC) Sync and joined the session immediately — even while 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘷𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯 𝘢𝘶𝘵𝘰.

As someone who has been involved with the open-source community, WikiTech, Open Knowledge Foundation, Road to Wiki, and Wikimedia contributions for quite some time, this session was genuinely valuable for me.

𝗜 𝗴𝗼𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘀𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗴𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗺𝘆 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗳:
• The Universal Code of Conduct (UCoC) and why it matters across the Wikimedia movement.
• Expected and unacceptable behaviours within Wikimedia communities.
• How respectful, constructive, and inclusive collaboration is maintained.
• How UCoC violations are handled and where community members can seek support.
• The broader responsibility that comes with being part of an open-source and knowledge-sharing ecosystem.

𝗜 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮𝗹𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗮 𝗹𝗼𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗮-𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶 𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀, 𝗴𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀, 𝗽𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁, 𝘀𝗼 𝗴𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗮 𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝗹 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗴𝗼𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘁𝗲 𝗱𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝗰𝗼𝘀𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺. 😄

For me, this session felt more like a 𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 + 𝗽𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 — a chance to revisit concepts I have already encountered while contributing and to understand them from a community perspective.

And honestly, that is what I like about the Wikimedia ecosystem. There is always something new to learn, even when you think you already know the basics.

A big thank you to Ankit Sir, @Sneha Ma

description:
𝗜 𝗮𝗺 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗺𝘆 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻-𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗯𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗲𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶𝗖𝗹𝘂𝗯 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮 – 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁 (𝗝𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘆–𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗲 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲), published by The Open Knowledge Initiatives - India (OKI), International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad (IIITH) 

The report highlights technical contributions made by participants of the #RoadtoWiki program to the Wikimedia Foundation ecosystem, documenting production-ready patches that have been reviewed, approved, and merged across multiple Wikimedia repositories.

Over the last six months, I have consistently contributed to the Wikimedia ecosystem, submitting patches across multiple repositories.
Contributing to Wikimedia has given me invaluable experience working with large-scale production codebases, professional code review workflows, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, debugging, and collaborating with developers from the global open-source community.

This recognition is an important milestone in my learning journey. More importantly, it reinforces the value of continuous learning, collaborative development, and building software that benefits millions of users around the world.

I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to Wikiclub Tech India (Part of OKI-IIITH), WikiClub Tech-UIT and Ankit Sir for organizing initiatives like #Road_to_Wiki across multiple colleges and cities. These programs are creating incredible opportunities for students to contribute to world-class open-source projects and learn industry-standard software engineering practices.

A special thank you to my mentors and seniors who supported me throughout this journey. Your technical guidance, detailed code reviews, constructive feedback, and constant encouragement helped me grow as an open-source contributor.

Special thanks to:
Sanskar, Mohd, Shivaansh, Reeti, Adarsh, Sarthak,T Ebenezer, Jagadeeshwar, and the entire WikiClubTech_MUJ Tech mentors, Trusted Testers, reviewers, and #Wikimedia community for sharing your knowledge and always being willing to help.

This achievement would not have been possible without your support.
I look forward to continuing my open-source journey, contributing to impactful projects, and learning from this amazing community.

description:
🚀 𝗥𝗼𝗮𝗱 𝗧𝗼 𝗪𝗶𝗸𝗶 𝗖𝗼𝗵𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝟮 — 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗦𝗤𝗟 & 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹-𝗪𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱 𝗦𝘆𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗺𝘀
Today’s #RoadToWiki session was honestly one of the most engaging and inspiring technical sessions I’ve attended recently. The way concepts were taught made even complex topics feel simple, practical, and easy to connect with real-world development.
This session mainly focused on #SQL, databases, and the architecture behind scalable web systems. Since I have already built and hosted several websites before, I could relate to many concepts, but today I learned how these things actually work at the production level in large-scale platforms like Wikimedia Foundation.
Some major learnings from today:
🔹 Difference between SQL and #NoSQL databases and when to use each
🔹 Database schema design, normalization, #CRUD operations, and scalability concepts
🔹 How production systems manage huge traffic using caching and optimized architectures
🔹 Practical understanding of Redis, Varnish, #Elasticsearch, and master-replica database systems
🔹 Importance of proper table relationships and clean database structures for maintainability
What made this session special was the way every topic was connected to practical use cases instead of only theory.
A huge thank you to Vrijraj Singh sir for such an amazing teaching style and practical explanations throughout the session. The way he explained databases, system design, and web architecture made learning genuinely enjoyable.
It was also inspiring to learn about Vrijraj Singh Sir’s journey and achievements, especially being featured by GOOGLE INDIA and the Google Developers Group community. His story was truly motivating for students and developers who want to grow in tech and open source 🚀

Special thanks to Ankit Kumar Verma Sir for explaining how Wikipedia started, how it evolved, and how such a massive #collaborative ecosystem works behind the scenes. That part was really inspiring and gave a new perspective on open-source contribution.
Also thankful to Wikiclub Tech India and the entire Wikimedia Foundation community for organizing such valuable sessions and helping students learn real engineering concepts beyond college academics 🙌
